endorsements.quote: Document which approach is used for each AI system and any gaps that remain.

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: For each detected error, what is the probability that the error will be corrected?

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Acceptable failure behaviors (‘failsafes’) in the clinical environment should also be established, taking into account workflow, environment, and stakeholder considerations.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Define mitigation measures to be applied after deployment | Warnings to the users, system shutdown, reprocessing of the input data, acquisition of new input data, use of an alternative procedure, or human judgment only

endorsements.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reducing Dispensing Errors for Patient Safety and Quality: A Systems Approach
endorsements.quote: To ensure interoperability and operational resilience, systems should be engineered for robust connections with e-prescribing, EHR, and dispensing platforms, with defined fail-safe modes, latency budgets, and error-recovery protocols that preserve safe operations during outages or degraded performance, and with technical service-level objectives aligned with clinical safety goals.

endorsements.title: Drone-delivered automated external defibrillators in prehospital emergency care: implementation evidence, bottlenecks, and conceptual integration with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications
endorsements.quote: The integrated system should also include fail-safe design and operational redundancy, so that failure of any single component does not interrupt the chain of survival.

evidence.title: Pro-active risk analysis of an in-house developed deep learning based autoplanning tool for breast Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.effect: Case-specific QA lowered lack-of-detectability from 8.17 to 3.51 and risk from Tolerable to Acceptable.
evidence.quote: The case-specific QA report was chosen as a barrier against the ‘prediction is bad’ failure mode (see Table 3 ), which decreased the lack of detectability score.

evidence.title: Risk assessment and quality management in AIO based on CT-linac for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: An improved FMEA and FTA approach
evidence.effect: Mean RPN was 55.80 ± 38.40 without QM and 16.17 ± 10.99 with QM.
evidence.quote: The results showed that the RPN for the QM‐free group was 55.80 ± 38.40, and for the QM group was 16.17 ± 10.99.

evidence.title: Architectural Safety Mechanisms for Multi-Agent Clinical LLM Systems Under Knowledge Base Distribution Shift
evidence.effect: Stateful graph maintained GCS = 1.00 across all shift conditions through a regime-aware safety floor.
evidence.quote: The stateful graph architecture maintained GCS = 1.00 across all shift conditions through its regime-aware safety floor, which operates independently of retrieval quality.

evidence.title: DiagnosticXchange: an open-source framework for evaluating safety, efficiency, and diagnostic reasoning in clinical AI systems
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Unsafe AI behaviors: premature diagnosis and futile invasive procedures
evidence.effect: Premature diagnosis up to 9.3%, noncontributory invasive procedures 8.7%-29.9%, futile invasive procedures on failed cases 3.7%-18.1%.
evidence.quote: Safety analysis revealed premature diagnosis (up to 9.3%), noncontributory invasive procedures (8.7%-29.9%), and futile invasive procedures on failed cases (3.7%-18.1%).

commentary.bottom_line: Three offline or simulated studies suggest that structured failure-mode analysis with quality assurance, or a built-in safety floor, may lower estimated risk from AI errors. No study measured whether these fail-safes kept errors from reaching real patients, so certainty is very low.

perspectives.view: Two failure mode analyses and one synthetic benchmark tested the practice. Mean risk priority number fell from 55.80 to 16.17 with quality management, and lack-of-detectability fell from 8.17 to 3.51 with case-specific QA. These are team-rated scores or synthetic outcomes without patient data, so indirectness and risk of bias are serious.

The hazard study found premature diagnosis in up to 9.3% of LLM sessions and futile invasive procedures in 3.7% to 18.1% of failed cases, which shows errors can proceed without a stop. A safety floor held guideline compliance at 1.00 across all shift conditions in synthetic patients, which suggests fail-safe design may contain such errors.

Both failure mode analyses were done offline by review teams rating hypothetical failures. Neither reports the time, staffing, or workflow changes that case-specific QA required in routine use, and neither measured whether errors were actually detected and corrected at the rated rates after go-live.

Seven sources endorse the practice. NIST AI 600-1 asks that systems fail safely when operating beyond their knowledge limits, and the CHAI playbook asks health systems to document the approach used and any remaining gaps. The supplied sources are voluntary frameworks, professional statements, and commentaries rather than binding requirements.

None of the three tests reports patient demographics, payer mix, language, or literacy, and one used only synthetic patients. The studies therefore cannot show whether error detection and fail-safes perform equally for the patients a safety-net system serves.

FUTURE-AI lists fallback measures that include warnings to users, system shutdown, and reliance on human judgment only. No supplied study measured whether patients reached a clinician when an AI system failed, or how patients viewed those fallbacks.

commentary.research_gap: Prospective studies in live clinical settings should measure how often AI errors are detected and corrected before they reach patients, compare fail-safe designs with usual practice, and report staffing cost and patient outcomes, including results for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, and low-literacy populations.
commentary.underserved_note: No test included or reported Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations; two studies analyzed failure modes rather than patients, and one used synthetic patients. Health systems serving these groups have no direct evidence that the reported risk reductions apply to their patients.
